Picture the accountability group. The circle of chairs. The coffee going cold in paper cups. The same men, same confessions, same Tuesday night, same year it was last year. Someone reads a scripture. Someone cries. The pastor calls it a spiritual battle. The therapist calls it attachment dysregulation. The productivity influencer calls it a dopamine problem.

None of them call it what it is.

An extraction operation with a business model.

Pornography is not a private moral failure any more than a landmine is a private safety concern. The framing of privacy is itself part of the design. Keep it personal. Keep it shameful. Keep it between you and your accountability partner and your cycle of confession and relapse and confession again. The loop is the product. The loop keeps you just broken enough to stay manageable.

What the ancient record understood, and what every institutional overlay since has worked to bury, is that this is not new. The targeting of male generative force is not a feature of the digital age. It is the oldest extraction play in the archive.

Azazel’s Curriculum, Updated for Broadband

The ancient world did not speak about seed the way we do. It did not reduce it to biology. The concentrated generative capacity of a man was understood as the same force that builds civilizations, raises sons, lights fires, starts movements. To drain that force into simulation was not a moral inconvenience. It was a category of warfare.

1 Enoch documents the systematic targeting of human generative force as the primary vector of pre-Flood disruption. The Watchers did not simply interbreed with humanity. They taught. They transmitted. They showed men how to redirect creative force into spectacle, simulation, and appetite. The specific corruptions listed in chapters 8 and 69 are a curriculum. Cosmetics to distort the image. Weaponry to redirect violence inward. The art of written enchantment to trap attention in loops it cannot exit.

What is running now is the industrial version of that same curriculum.

The pipe changed shape. The content evolved. The distance from cave to server farm crossed in ten thousand years. But the operational logic is identical: find the generative force, build a pipe toward it, and drain it into something that produces nothing except more appetite and more drainage. The man on the other end of the pipe doesn’t build anything. He doesn’t resist anything. He doesn’t threaten anything.

He generates revenue for someone else’s extraction operation and calls it a private struggle.

Your Shame Is Also a Revenue Stream

The church built an accountability industrial complex on top of this operation, and whether it did so consciously is almost beside the point. The effect is the same: shame as a management system. Confession loops that never produce liberation, only more shame, more confession, more dependency on the institution that processes your failure.

Atrophy. The form of moral concern with none of the bone for actual restoration. Men who are simultaneously guilty and non-threatening. Men who occupy themselves with the administration of their own brokenness instead of the construction of anything real. The accountability group meets every Tuesday. The same men. The same chairs. The coffee going cold.

Then the other side of the institutional failure. The progressive liberation frame built a mirror operation. Sex work is work. The body is a commodity like any other commodity. Desire is identity, consumption is freedom, normalization is justice. This frame convinced men that their extraction is actually their expression. That the drainage is self-actualization. That the pipeline running their generative force into a server farm somewhere is a form of personal liberation.

Chaos. The abandonment of any root at all. The man who consumes without guilt is not free. He is just drained without friction.

The confession booth and the subscription feed are two nodes in the same harvest network. One processes your shame. One processes your drive. Both leave you empty. Both leave you manageable. Neither was designed to produce a man with intact generative force, because a man with intact generative force is the one thing both systems cannot absorb.

He Is Already Neutralized

The operation is worth understanding precisely, because precision is what makes recognition possible.

When generative drive is repeatedly redirected into a screen, the reward wiring of the brain rebuilds itself around a specific lie: maximum arousal, zero output. Zero risk. Zero relationship. Zero cost. Zero consequence. The nervous system learns to associate the deepest biological signals with the production of absolutely nothing. It becomes incapable of tolerating the friction that building anything real requires.

A business requires tolerating uncertainty for months before any return. A family requires tolerating conflict, mess, demand, the sheer weight of sustained presence. A resistance requires tolerating danger with no guaranteed outcome. These are precisely the tolerances that atrophy first.

A man wired for maximum arousal at zero cost cannot sustain the low-friction boredom of meaningful work. He cannot sit with the unresolved tension of a real relationship long enough for it to deepen. He cannot absorb the slow-building discomfort of any project whose payoff is measured in years. His reward wiring has been calibrated to the screen. Everything else feels like deprivation.

Babylon does not need to arrest a man like that. He is already neutralized. He sits in the chair generating profit for the extraction operation while his creative capacity drains into a server farm. He is not a threat to any system. He is a revenue stream for the system that broke him.

Reroute the Current

The narrow path is not moral management. It is not a better accountability group, a stricter filter, a more disciplined confession schedule. Moral management is still operating inside the extraction system’s frame. It accepts the premise that this is a private spiritual battle, and it offers you better tools to lose it more slowly.

The first move is recognition. Not remorse. Recognition. You are inside an active extraction operation. It has a business model. It has institutional cover on both the religious and secular flanks. It was running before you were born and it will run after you die. You did not invent the pipe it built toward you. You did not design the reward wiring it hijacked. You are not uniquely weak because it worked on you.

But you are responsible for what you do with the recognition.

The second move is redirection, not just cessation. You do not simply stop the drain. You reroute the current. Generative force does not disappear when you cut off the extraction pipe. It accumulates. The question is whether it accumulates toward something you are building, or whether it finds the next available drain.

This is why the ninety-day rebuild is not about abstinence. Abstinence is a vacuum. Vacuums collapse.

The rebuild is about directed output. Building something with the creative force that the extraction system was designed to harvest. A business. A body. A body of work. A family. A community that does not depend on Babylon’s supply lines for its existence.

The man who comes out the other side of that process is not more moral in the way the accountability group means moral. He is not softer or more contrite or better at confession. He is more dangerous. Specifically dangerous. To every system that needed him empty.

The circle of chairs meets again next Tuesday. The coffee will be the same temperature. The confessions will be recognizable. The pastor will say spiritual battle. The therapist will say attachment dysregulation.

And somewhere in a data center, a quarterly earnings report will document exactly how much generative force was successfully converted into revenue last month.

The only man Babylon cannot govern is the one who stopped feeding it his creative force and started building something it cannot own.
